title: Circles, Part 3: Traps and the Fast Way

beats.say: In this video, we look at five mistakes students make with circles, and then use Desmos to find the center of a circle from its equation, and to test whether a point lies on it.
Each trap is shown as a wrong line first, then the right line, with the reason it's so tempting.
Trap one. In x minus three, squared, plus y plus one, squared, equals sixty-four, the right side is r squared, not r.
Take the square root. The radius is the square root of sixty-four, which is eight.

scenes.title: Trap 2: the sign of the center

beats.say: Trap two. In x plus five, squared, the center has the opposite sign of the number in the parentheses. Students read the sign as written.
The factor x plus five is x minus negative five. So the x coordinate of the center is negative five.
Trap three. When you complete the squares, the amounts you add must also be added to the right side. Students add them only on the left.
Add twenty-five and four to both sides. Seven plus twenty-five plus four is thirty-six, so the right side is thirty-six.
Trap four. A circle with a diameter of fourteen has a radius of seven. Students put the diameter into pi r squared.
Halve the diameter first. With a radius of seven, the area is pi times seven squared, which is forty-nine pi.
Trap five. An inscribed angle intercepting an arc of one hundred forty degrees isn't one hundred forty degrees. Students treat it as a central angle.
beats.wrong_why: Only a central angle equals its arc

beats.say: An inscribed angle is half of its intercepted arc. So it measures seventy degrees.
Desmos graphs circle equations in any form, expanded or not. You can type the equation exactly as given, and read the center and the radius from the grid.
For arcs and sectors, skip Desmos. Write the fraction of the circle, multiply, and keep answers in terms of pi.
Open a fresh graph. We'll type the circle from the hard example exactly as it was given, without completing the square.
Type x squared plus y squared plus ten x minus four y equals seven. Press the right arrow after each exponent.
Desmos draws the circle. The leftmost and rightmost points are a diameter apart, so the center is exactly halfway between them.
Now plot the center we found, negative five comma two. The point sits in the middle of the circle.
To test a point, type it. The point one comma two sits exactly on the circle, six units to the right of the center, which confirms the radius of six.
Now a practice problem. A circle has a radius of twelve. Find the length of the arc cut off by a central angle of one hundred fifty degrees. Pause the video, try it, and then watch the solution.
The arc is a fraction of the circumference. The fraction is one hundred fifty over three hundred sixty, which reduces to five twelfths. The circumference is two pi times twelve.
One hundred fifty over three hundred sixty reduces to five twelfths, and two pi times twelve is twenty-four pi.
Five twelfths of twenty-four is ten. So the arc length is ten pi.
To recap. The right side of a circle equation is r squared, and the center has the opposite signs of the parentheses.
beats.item: Right side is r²; center has opposite signs

beats.say: Add completed squares to both sides, use the radius and not the diameter, and halve an intercepted arc for an inscribed angle.
beats.item: Both sides; radius; half the arc

beats.say: That completes the Math topics. Next, we begin the Reading and Writing topics, starting with central ideas and details.
